label: Tower value separation
query: How should Tower separate value-at-stake, committed value, measuring value, and realized savings for the Kyriba program?
answer: For Kyriba at Lakeshore, Tower needs four clearly distinct buckets, each with different evidence and owners. I’d structure them like this: 1) Value-at-stake (the “ceiling”) • What it is: The full, risk-adjusted opportunity based on Kyriba’s design scope – e.g., better cash visibility, reduced idle balances, lower FX/interest costs, bank fee rationalization, process FTE capacity. • How to treat it in Tower: – Tie each line to a Kyriba capability (e.g., in-house banking, cash pooling, payment factory). – Make explicit assumptions (rates, volumes, behavior changes) and tag sources (Treasury analysis, vendor BAFO, peer benchmarks). – This should align with LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026 Strategy / BAFO artifacts, not execution data. 2) Committed value (the “contract” with the business) • What it is: The subset of value-at-stake that Treasury, Finance, and IT jointly sign up to deliver in this first Kyriba release sequence, with timing. • How to treat it in Tower: – Only include use cases backed by: (a) funded Kyriba scope, and (b) explicit business-owner commitment (e.g., Treasurer, Corporate Controller). – Represent as time-phased targets: “By Q4 FY26: $X annual bank fee savings; Q2 FY27: $Y working capital interest benefit,” etc. – Governance hook: any movement from “at-stake” to “committed” should be traceable to a decision record (SteerCo minutes, approval memo). 3) Measuring value (the “instrumentation and proof plan”) • What it is: How Lakeshore will actually observe whether Kyriba is on track to deliver committed value.
